key_insight: Purely amorphous In-Zn-O thin films can act as both transparent conductive layers and effective Cu diffusion barriers, with best performance near Zn/(In+Zn) ≈ 0.12 and intermediate oxygen deficiency.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable route to replace silver metallization with copper in solar cells while protecting silicon absorbers from Cu contamination.
method: 2D combinatorial sputtering screened Zn/(In+Zn) ratio and oxygen content in one materials library
7 nm ultrathin In-Zn-O films were deposited on Si without intentional substrate heating
Cu-overlayer stacks were annealed at 200–450°C and assessed via copper silicide formation plus Si photoluminescence
evidence_signal: Cu ingress was not detected for most In-Zn-O compositions even after 20 h at 200°C, while unprotected Si/Cu stacks lost photoluminescence in under 1 h; Cu silicides appeared only after crystallization at 450°C and above.
watch_item: Barrier performance depends on maintaining the film amorphous state, so thermal crystallization during processing could weaken protection.
paper_title: Accelerated development of amorphous InZnO thin films as transparent conductive Cu diffusion barriers
